label: Transit (bus / rail)
description: A public transit agency: bus routes, light-rail lines, depots and yards, an operations control center with CAD/AVL, fare collection, transit police. Plans: the PTASP (49 CFR 673), State Safety Oversight notification (49 CFR 674), and for rail systems the TSA cybersecurity directive (SD 1582-21-01E: Cybersecurity Coordinator, incident response plan exercised annually, CISA report within 72 hours).

vocabulary.facility: the transit system (routes, lines, stops, stations, depots and the control center)
vocabulary.frontline: bus operators, train operators, dispatchers, street supervisors, mechanics, station agents

it: fare collection and smart-card back office
rider app and real-time arrivals feed (GTFS-RT)
ot: on-board vehicle logic units and AVL radios
rail signalling and train control (wayside signals, CBTC, PTC)
fuel management and depot building automation
tunnel ventilation and fire life safety
fare gates and ticket vending machines

roles.name: Director of Transportation (Incident Commander)
roles.description: Owns service delivery: dispatch, operators, routes and lines.

roles.name: IT / OT Systems Manager (Technical Lead)
roles.description: Owns CAD/AVL, fare systems, networks and the investigation.

roles.name: Communications Director (Public Information Officer)
roles.description: Owns rider alerts, social media, the press and the website.

roles.name: Chief of Transit Police (Security)
roles.description: Owns safety and security on vehicles, at stations and depots.

roles.name: Director of Fleet Maintenance
roles.description: Owns the vehicles, the depots and the mechanics.

roles.name: Chief Safety Officer
roles.description: Owns safety event classification, the two-hour FTA / SSOA notification and stop-work authority.

roles.name: Cybersecurity Coordinator (CISO)
roles.description: The TSA-designated coordinator: declares the cyber incident, reports to CISA, runs the incident response plan.

outsideParties: FTA (Federal Transit Administration; two-hour notification of qualifying rail safety events)
TSA Surface Operations (significant security concerns within 24 hours)
CISA (TSA-required cyber incident report within 72 hours)
FBI (JTTF) and the regional fusion center
mediaChannels: rider posts on X/Twitter with photos of stuck buses

sceneAnchors.public: at a busy bus transit center: articulated city buses at numbered bays, riders with bags waiting under shelters, a dark arrivals screen as a plain rectangle, daylight
sceneAnchors.control: inside a transit operations control center: a curved console with dispatchers wearing headsets, a large wall of dark map screens, muted blue lighting
sceneAnchors.exterior: a city bus stopped on an urban street with its hazard lights on, riders standing on the sidewalk, a supervisor SUV behind it, daylight

noiseExamples: a farebox jammed with a folded bill
a depot fuel pump printing blank receipts
an operator asking for a schedule swap
a broken wheelchair lift on one coach
pressureExamples: a rider tweet with a photo of buses bunched at a stop
a Facebook post claiming a bus was hijacked
a reporter asking why the real-time app shows ghost buses
a city council aide asking for a statement before the evening news
the union steward demanding operators be pulled in
the TSA 72-hour clock for the CISA cyber incident report running
the two-hour FTA and SSOA notification after a derailment
